cover letter
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)
Master's degree in public health, social work, or related area. (Preferred)
Strong working skills and experience implementing qualitative methodologies and approaches, qualitative interviewing, qualitative data analysis.

Experience working on issues such as sexual and/or intimate partner violence, gender equity, sexual and reproductive health and with the following populations: LGBTQ+ youth, racially/ethnically minoritized youth, and survivors of sexual or intimate partner violence in the U.S.
Experience leading and/or ability to learn how to lead qualitative analysis using qualitative analysis software, such as Dedoose or Atlas.ti.
Experience developing and managing and/or ability to learn how to develop and manage research protocols for implementation and for IRB submissions.

The Boyce Research Group at the University of California Berkeley School of Public Health is seeking a Qualitative Research Manager to lead the qualitative components of multiple research projects focused on LGBTQ+, racial/ethnic minoritized, and other marginalized youth. These projects focus on sexual and dating violence prevention, healthy relationships, and access to support services and are being conducted in partnership with the California Department of Public Health, Stop It Now!, the Center on Violence Prevention Research, ValorUS, and the National LGBTQ Institute on Intimate Partner Violence, among others. The role will be supervised by Dr. Sabrina Boyce and will be responsible for managing qualitative components of multiple research projects. Qualitative research management includes IRB protocol development and submissions, instrument development, scheduling and conducting interviews using a trauma-informed and survivor-centered approach, processing and storing data confidentially, training and leading a small team in conducting data collection and analysis, and managing participant incentives. This role will contribute to literature reviews, development of scientific manuscripts and practitioner-facing dissemination materials. Under supervision of the PI, this role will participate in preparing grant proposals and identifying new funding sources. Additionally, this role will manage at least one research-practice partnership, ensuring a positive working relationship and timely submission of deliverables, and facilitate a youth research advisory board to elicit youth feedback on research protocols and results.
Independently manages at least one research-practice partnership, leading meetings weekly with the partner, ensuring a positive collaborative relationship, and timely submission of deliverables.
Track and ensure timely completion of deliverables.
Analyzes research data and interprets results using rigorous methods and integrity.
Presents results to the research team for discussion and interpretation, and presents results to practitioner and scientific audiences.

Utilize rigorous research methodology and trauma-informed, survivor-centered approaches to conduct data collection and interact with research participants, including youth who experience marginalization based on their identity and service providers who work with such youth.
Plans qualitative data collection, including the design of survey instruments and determining the sampling and reporting procedures.
Manage the administration of participant incentives, including tracking and sending incentives to participants and managing this aspect of the budget.
Draft academic manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals, both for systematic reviews and for original research, and submit to appropriate journals.
Lead the drafting and development of funder-facing, practitioner-facing, and community-facing products, briefs, social media shareables, and reports.
Integrate feedback from the PI and funder for finalization.

Facilitate the Youth Research Advisory Board, engaging with youth in a reciprocal relationship that includes eliciting their feedback on protocols and instruments and on interpretation of results using principles of youth empowerment and mutual learning.

Conduct systematic literature reviews to summarize current research and identify gaps in the literature to inform data collection efforts, anchor research methodologies in best practices, manuscript development, and grant proposal development.
Develops proposals and recommendations to guide and support a broader strategic direction for the research team.
Collaborates on the design, documentation, testing, and implementation of research studies.
Participates in workshops, trainings, and other professional development activities; may participate in committees, projects, and other service activities.
Other duties, as assigned.
Working knowledge of public health research, public health theories and frameworks around health equity, data collection and analysis.
Advanced project management skills and demonstrated problem solving skills.
Demonstrated ability to develop publishable research/academic manuscripts from public health research results.
Demonstrated ability to respectfully engage youth and/or community member voices in research.

Excellent interpersonal and communication skills to interact with a variety of personalities at all levels of the organization and cross-cultures, work effectively as a member of a research team; and in establishing and maintaining effective working relationships with staff of all levels, funders, and community partners.
Ability to multi-task with demanding timeframes.
Ability to manage secure data collection, implement voluntary consent protocols, and maintain all confidentiality.
Strong analytical and critical thinking skills to identify problems and develop innovative solutions.
